# Contributing to this project

Thanks for contributing to the FTC 7129 Robo Raiders' BioBuzz project! Please follow the steps
below when submitting changes.

## 1. Create a Local Branch

Make your changes on a separate local branch rather than directly on `main`.

Choose a descriptive branch name that reflects the work you're doing. Replace `your-branch-name`
below with a suitable branch name for your changes

```bash
git checkout -b your-branch-name
```

## 2. Commit and Push Your Changes

Commit your changes locally, then push your branch to GitHub. Replace `Describe your changes`
below with a description of what you did. Replace `your-branch-name` with the name of your branch
from the previous step.

```bash
git add -A
git commit -m "Describe your changes"
git push -u origin your-branch-name
```

## 3. Submit a Pull Request

Once your branch has been pushed, open a pull request (PR) on GitHub.

**Important: Make sure your pull request targets the `main` branch of our team's repository
unless you have reason to put a PR into another target branch.**

Before submitting your PR, verify the following:

- [ ] Your changes are on the desired non-main branch.
- [ ] Changes from the branch have been pushed to GitHub.
- [ ] The base branch for the PR is `main`.
- [ ] Your PR includes a clear description of the changes.

## 4. Another Team Member Reviews and Merges the Code

Another team member should then review the PR. If they approve, they can either approve in the
Github UI and let you know to merge it. Or alternatively, if they approve, they can merge it
themselves. If they have questions/suggestions, they can make those directly in the PR.

_NOTE: PR approval is not actually required; the person who submits a change can merge their
own PR. However, it's best practice to have someone else review your code so they can
add feedback if they see something worth changing. They can also learn new things by reviewing your
code_
